one_liner: Netlify is a hosted web deployment platform with a broad public REST API and an official MCP server.

auth.notes: Public integrations acting on behalf of users must use OAuth 2.0. Personal access tokens are documented for scripts and other direct API calls.

access.notes: The pricing page says the free plan is always free, and a developer guide says you can generate a PAT in your user settings. Nothing quoted restricts API credentials to a paid plan, approval, or sales, so self-serve free access is inferred rather than explicit.

api.notes: The public OpenAPI reference documents read and write operations for sites, builds, deploys and rollbacks, environment variables, DNS, and team membership, as well as read operations for form submissions.

mcp.notes: Netlify offers a hosted server and the local @netlify/mcp package. The server can create projects, deploy code, and manage project configuration. Netlify recommends the hosted server for the latest capabilities.

verdict.rationale: Credentials are self-serve and free, and the documented API is broad enough to be useful.

evidence.quote: If you’re making a public integration with Netlify for others to enjoy, you must use OAuth2.
Use your PAT for manual authentication in shell scripts or commands that use the Netlify API.
The free plan is always free, with hard monthly limits that cannot be exceeded or incur any costs.
If you’re deploying on behalf of a single user, or users that won’t need to claim their site on Netlify, you can generate a PAT in your user settings.

Netlify is a hosting service for the programmable web. It understands your documents and provides an API to handle atomic deploys of websites, manage form submissions, inject JavaScript snippets, and much more.
This is a REST-style API that uses JSON for serialization and OAuth 2 for authentication.
The official Netlify MCP Server is available now.
Agents can now create projects, deploy applications, and manage your infrastructure using natural language prompts.
Our recommendation is to use the remote MCP server to have the most up-to-date version of the MCP capabilities.

problems: Netlify’s pricing and authentication pages establish the Free plan and the token workflow separately, but the retrieved text did not explicitly tie Free to credential eligibility. No authenticated Free-plan test was performed.
The Composio catalog search returned no Netlify match. The expected toolkit page could not be read, and the fetch error did not distinguish a missing page from a blocked or client-rendered page.

verification.note: OAuth2 is required for public integrations, and PATs are documented for direct API use.
Self-serve free access is inferred from the always-free plan and the ability to generate a PAT in user settings; the quotes do not explicitly tie PAT creation to the free plan.
The public reference calls it a REST-style API. Broad coverage is an acceptable estimate, though the quotes do not establish the specific operations listed in the notes.
A Netlify page says its official server is available now. The quotes do not establish the local package claim or the exact server URL.
No claim was made, so there is nothing to check.
Inferred self-serve free credentials and a documented, useful REST API support buildable_now with no stated blocker.
